# 2. Microbial diversity and community succession

## 2.1 Beta-diversity

```{r beta-diversity}
# Figure 2A
# SD vs SI PCoA (Bray-Curtis)
# + SI year gradient + centroid trajectory
# + PERMANOVA + PERMDISP

# SD vs SI PCoA (Bray-Curtis)
# + SI year gradient
# + SD/SI ellipses
# + PERMANOVA (only)
# + prevalence filter: >=10% non-zero in SD+SI

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(vegan)
  library(stringr)
})

# 1) Load data 
infile <- file.path(data_dir, "Desktop", "replot", "meta", "species_all_acpm.txt")

df <- read.delim(
  infile,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE,
  row.names = 1,
  header = TRUE,
  sep = "\t"
)

stopifnot(all(c("kind", "year") %in% colnames(df)))

# 2) Keep SD & SI only
target_years <- c("11", "12", "14", "15", "17")   

df_sub <- df %>%
  filter(kind %in% c("SD", "SI")) %>%
  mutate(
    kind = factor(kind, levels = c("SD", "SI")),
    year_chr = str_trim(as.character(year))
  ) %>%
  
 
  filter(kind == "SD" | (kind == "SI" & year_chr %in% target_years)) %>%
  mutate(
    year_chr = factor(year_chr, levels = target_years),
    #  ellipse 
    group2 = kind
  )

# 3) Build abundance matrix + prevalence filter 
meta_cols <- intersect(c("group", "kind", "year", "year_chr", "group2"), colnames(df_sub))
otu <- df_sub %>% select(-all_of(meta_cols))

otu_mat <- as.matrix(otu)
mode(otu_mat) <- "numeric"
otu_mat[is.na(otu_mat)] <- 0

# Remove all-zero species first (optional)
otu_mat <- otu_mat[, colSums(otu_mat) > 0, drop = FALSE]

# Prevalence filter: keep species present (non-zero) in >=10% samples (within SD+SI subset)
prev_cutoff <- 0.10
n_samples <- nrow(otu_mat)
min_n_nonzero <- ceiling(prev_cutoff * n_samples)

nonzero_counts <- colSums(otu_mat > 0)
keep_cols <- nonzero_counts >= min_n_nonzero
otu_mat <- otu_mat[, keep_cols, drop = FALSE]

cat("Samples (SD+SI):", n_samples, "\n")
cat("Species kept (>=10% non-zero):", ncol(otu_mat), "\n")

# 4) Bray-Curtis distance 
dist_bc <- vegdist(otu_mat, method = "bray")

# 5) PCoA (cmdscale) 
pcoa <- cmdscale(dist_bc, k = 2, eig = TRUE)

coords <- as.data.frame(pcoa$points)
colnames(coords) <- c("Dim1", "Dim2")
coords$sample <- rownames(coords)

# variance explained (approx, using positive eigenvalues)
eig <- pcoa$eig
eig_pos <- eig[eig > 0]
var_exp <- eig_pos / sum(eig_pos)
dim1_pct <- round(100 * var_exp[1], 2)
dim2_pct <- round(100 * var_exp[2], 2)

plot_df <- df_sub %>%
  mutate(sample = rownames(df_sub)) %>%
  left_join(coords, by = "sample") %>%
  mutate(
    fill_key = ifelse(kind == "SD", "SD", paste0("SI-", as.character(year_chr))),
    fill_key = factor(fill_key, levels = c("SD", paste0("SI-", target_years)))
  )

# 6) PERMANOVA and multivariate dispersion (SD vs SI) 
meta_test <- plot_df %>%
  dplyr::select(sample, group2) %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("sample")

# Ensure that metadata order matches the distance matrix
meta_test <- meta_test[rownames(as.matrix(dist_bc)), , drop = FALSE]

# PERMANOVA
adon <- vegan::adonis2(
  dist_bc ~ group2,
  data = meta_test,
  permutations = 999
)

adon_p  <- adon$`Pr(>F)`[1]
adon_r2 <- adon$R2[1]

# Homogeneity of multivariate dispersion
dispersion <- vegan::betadisper(
  dist_bc,
  group = factor(meta_test$group2)
)

dispersion_test <- vegan::permutest(
  dispersion,
  permutations = 999
)

dispersion_p <- dispersion_test$tab$`Pr(>F)`[1]

# Annotation
anno_text <- paste0(
  "PERMANOVA\n",
  "P = ", format.pval(adon_p, digits = 3, eps = 0.001), "\n",
  "R\u00B2 = ", sprintf("%.4f", adon_r2), "\n",
  "Dispersion P = ",
  format.pval(dispersion_p, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
)

anno_text


aggregate(
  dispersion$distances,
  by = list(Group = dispersion$group),
  FUN = mean
)

# annotation placement (bottom-right)
x_rng <- range(plot_df$Dim1, na.rm = TRUE)
y_rng <- range(plot_df$Dim2, na.rm = TRUE)
anno_x <- x_rng[2] - 0.02 * diff(x_rng)
anno_y <- y_rng[1] + 0.02 * diff(y_rng)

# 7) Colors 
# SD: brown；SI: 5-step green gradient (light->dark)
si_cols <- colorRampPalette(c("#dce775", "#33691e"))(length(target_years))
names(si_cols) <- paste0("SI-", target_years)

fill_cols <- c("SD" = "#ff9800", si_cols)



# ellipse colors（SD vs SI ）
ellipse_line_cols <- c("SD" = "#e65100", "SI" = "#1b5e20")  
ellipse_fill_cols <- c("SD" = "#ffcc80", "SI" = "#e6ee9c")  

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Dim1, y = Dim2)) +
  # points
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = fill_key),
    shape = 21, color = "white", stroke = 0.6,
    size = 3.5, alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  
  # filled ellipse (under) 
stat_ellipse(
  aes(group = group2, fill = group2),
  type = "t", level = 0.95,
  geom = "polygon",
  alpha = 0.18,          
  color = NA,            
  show.legend = FALSE
) +
  
  # outline ellipse (over) 
stat_ellipse(
  aes(group = group2, color = group2),
  type = "t", level = 0.95,
  geom = "path",
  linewidth = 0.8,       
  show.legend = FALSE
) +
  
  # scale for points
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = fill_cols,
    breaks = c("SD", paste0("SI-", target_years)),
    labels = c("SD", paste0("SI-", target_years)),
    name = "Group"
  ) +
  
  # scale for ellipse fill (SD/SI)
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(fill_cols, ellipse_fill_cols),
    breaks = c("SD", paste0("SI-", target_years)),
    labels = c("SD", paste0("SI-", target_years)),
    name = "Group"
  ) +
  
  # ellipse outline color
  scale_color_manual(values = ellipse_line_cols) +
  
  labs(
    x = paste0("Dim1 (", dim1_pct, "%)"),
    y = paste0("Dim2 (", dim2_pct, "%)")
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12,colour = "black"),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 12,colour = 'black')
  )
```

## 2.3 Alpha diversity
```{r alpha-diversity}

# calculate the index one by one
library(picante)
library(phyloseq)

#shannon index, base = exp(1)
shannon_index <- diversity(otu, index = 'shannon',base = exp(1)) # samples in row, features in column
head(shannon_index) 

# Gini-Simpson， also calle simpson
simpson <- diversity(otu, index = 'simpson')
head(simpson)

richness <- rowSums(otu > 0)
head(richness)

#Chao1 & ACE
#ACE
ace <- estimateR(otu)[4,]
head(ace)

nrow(shannon_index)
result <- data.frame(shannon_index, simpson, richness)

# alpha diversity was included in Table S1
```

## 2.4 Automatic labeling difference with a b c
```{r using_alpha_diversity_as_an_example}
#Construct a function to calculate the median for each group, perform Kruskal-Wallis and Behrens-Fisher tests to obtain significance, and manually determine the "abc" levels based on the median values and p-values.
 library(mvtnorm)
 library(reshape2)
 # library(npmc)
 library(ggplot2)

"npmc" <-
   function(dataset, control=NULL, df=2, alpha=0.05){
     mvtnorm <- require(mvtnorm, quietly=TRUE);
     if (!mvtnorm)
     {
       msg <- paste("npmc requires the mvtnorm-package to calculate",
                    "p-values for the test-statistics. This package is not",
                    "available on your system, so these values and the",
                    "confidence-limits will be missing values in the output!\n",
                    sep="\n");
       warning(msg);
     }
     
     if (any(df==0:2)) 
       dfm <- c(3,2,1)[df+1]
     else
     {
       warning("Wrong value for df\nUsing Satterthwaite t-approximation\n");
       dfm <- 1;
     }
     
     if (alpha<=0 || alpha>=1)
       stop("alpha must be a value between 0 and 1");
     
     
     name <- attr(dataset, "name");
     desc <- attr(dataset, "description");
     
     
     ## Function definitions 
     
     
    
     ## ssq:
     ## Calculates a vector's sum of squares
     
     ssq <- function(x) sum(x*x);
     
     ##
     ## force.ps: 
     ## Forces a matrix to be positive semidefinite by replacing 
     ## all negative eigenvalues by zero.
     ## 
     force.ps <- function(M.in)
     {
       eig <- eigen(M.in, symmetric=TRUE);
       spec <- eig$values;
       if (adjusted <- any(spec<0))
       {
         spec[spec<0] <- 0;
         M <- eig$vectors %*% diag(spec) %*% t(eig$vectors);
         ginv <- diag(1/sqrt(diag(M)));
         M.out <- ginv %*% M %*% ginv;
         ##if ((msg <- all.equal(M.in,M.out))!=TRUE) attr(M.out, "msg") <- msg;
       }
       else
       {
         M.out <- M.in;
       }
       attr(M.out,"adjusted") <- adjusted; 
       return (M.out);
     }
     
     
     ##
     ## z.dist:
     ## Calculates the p-values for the teststatistics using the mvtnorm-package.
     ## The 'sides' parameter determines whether the p-values for the one-
     ## or two-sided test are calculated.
     ## The statistic is supposed to follow a multivariate t-statistic with
     ## correlation-matrix 'corr' and 'df' degrees of freedom. If df=0, the
     ## multivariate normal-distribution is used.
     ## We use the mvtnorm-package by Frank Bretz (www.bioinf.uni-hannover.de) 
     ## to calculate the corresponding p-values. These algorithms originally 
     ## calculate the value P(X<=stat) for the mentioned multivariate distributions, 
     ## i.e. the 1-sided p-value. In order to gain the 2-sided p-value as well, 
     ## we used the algorithms on the absolute value of the teststatistic in 
     ## combination with the inflated correlation-matrix
     ##   kronecker(matrix(c(1,-1,-1,1),ncol=2), corr)
     ##
     z.dist <- function(stat, corr, df=0, sides=2)
     {
       if (!mvtnorm) return (NA);
       
       if (sides==2)
       {
         corr <- kronecker(matrix(c(1,-1,-1,1),ncol=2), corr);
         stat <- abs(stat);
       }
       n <- ncol(corr);
       sapply(stat, function(arg) 
       {
         pmvt(
           lower=rep(-Inf, n), 
           upper=rep(arg, n), 
           df=as.integer(df), 
           corr=corr, 
           delta=rep(0,n)
         )[1];
       });     
     } 
     
     
     ##
     ## z.quantile:
     ## Calculates the corresponding quantiles of z.dist p-values
     ## (used for the confidence-intervals)
     ##
     z.quantile <- function(p=0.95, start=0, corr, df=0, sides=2)
     {
       if (!mvtnorm) return (NA);
       
       if (z.dist(start,corr=corr,df=df,sides=sides) < p)
       {
         lower <- start;
         upper <- lower+1;
         while(z.dist(upper,corr=corr,df=df,sides=sides) < p)
           upper <- upper+1;
       }
       else
       {
         upper <- start;
         lower <- upper-1;
         while(z.dist(lower,corr=corr,df=df,sides=sides) > p)
           lower <- lower-1;
       }
       ur <- uniroot(f=function(arg) p-z.dist(arg,corr=corr,df=df,sides=sides),
                     upper=upper, lower=lower
       );
       ur$root;
     }
     
     
     ## Calculations 
     
     ## sort the dataset by factor
     dataset$class <- factor(dataset$class);
     datord <- order(dataset$class);
     attrs <- attributes(dataset);
     dataset <- data.frame(lapply(dataset, "[", datord));
     attributes(dataset) <- attrs;
     
     ## general data characteristics
     #attach(dataset);
     fl <- levels(dataset$class);             # factor-levels
     a <- nlevels(dataset$class);             # number of factor-levels
     samples <- base::split(dataset$var, dataset$class);    # split the data in separate sample-vectors
     n <- sapply(samples, length);    # sample sizes
     #detach(dataset);
     
     if (is.null(control))
     {
       ## create indexing vectors for the all-pairs situation
       tmp <- expand.grid(1:a, 1:a);
       ind <- tmp[[1]] > tmp[[2]];
       vi <- tmp[[2]][ind];
       vj <- tmp[[1]][ind];
     }
     else
     {
       ## create indexing vectors for the many-to-one situation
       if (!any(fl==control))
       {
         msg <- paste("Wrong control-group specification\n",
                      "The data does not contain a group with factor-level ",
                      control,
                      sep="");
         stop(msg, FALSE);
       }
       cg <- which(fl==control);
       vi <- which((1:a)!=cg);
       vj <- rep(cg, a-1);
     }
     
     ## number of comparisons ( a*(a-1)/2 for all-pairs, (a-1) for many-to-one )
     nc <- length(vi);              
     
     ## labels describing the compared groups 
     cmpid <- paste(vi, "-", vj, sep="");
     
     ## pairwise pooled sample-sizes
     gn <- n[vi]+n[vj];
     
     ## internal rankings
     intRanks <- lapply(samples, rank);
     
     ## pairwise rankings
     pairRanks <- lapply(1:nc, function(arg) 
     {
       rank(c(samples[[vi[arg]]], samples[[vj[arg]]]));  
     });
     
     ## estimators for the relative effects
     pd <- sapply(1:nc, function(arg)
     {
       i <- vi[arg]; 
       j <- vj[arg];
       (sum(pairRanks[[arg]][(n[i]+1):gn[arg]])/n[j]-(n[j]+1)/2)/n[i];  
     });
     
     ## Calculations for the BF-test 
     ##
     dij <- dji <- list(0);
     
     sqij <- sapply(1:nc, function(arg) 
     {
       i <- vi[arg]; 
       j <- vj[arg];
       pr <- pairRanks[[arg]][(n[i]+1):gn[arg]];
       dij[[arg]] <<- pr - sum(pr)/n[j] - intRanks[[j]] + (n[j]+1)/2;
       ssq(dij[[arg]])/(n[i]*n[i]*(n[j]-1));
     });
     
     sqji <- sapply(1:nc, function(arg)
     {
       i <- vi[arg];  
       j <- vj[arg];
       pr <- pairRanks[[arg]][1:n[i]];
       dji[[arg]] <<- pr - sum(pr)/n[i] - intRanks[[i]] + (n[i]+1)/2;
       ssq(dji[[arg]])/(n[j]*n[j]*(n[i]-1));
     });
     
     ## diagonal elements of the covariance-matrix
     vd.bf <- gn*(sqij/n[vj] + sqji/n[vi]);
     
     ## mark and correct zero variances for further calculations
     singular.bf <- (vd.bf==0);
     vd.bf[singular.bf] <- 0.00000001;
     
     ## standard-deviation
     std.bf <- sqrt(vd.bf/gn);
     
     ## teststatistic
     t.bf <- (pd-0.5)*sqrt(gn/vd.bf);
     
     ## Satterthwaite approxiamtion for the degrees of freedom
     df.sw <- (n[vi]*sqij + n[vj]*sqji)^2 / 
       ((n[vi]*sqij)^2/(n[vj]-1) + (n[vj]*sqji)^2/(n[vi]-1));
     df.sw[is.nan(df.sw)] <- Inf;
     
     ## choose degrees of freedom 
     df <- if (dfm<3) max(1, if (dfm==2) min(gn-2) else min(df.sw)) else 0;
     
     
     ## Calculations for the Steel-test 
     ##
     ## the Steel-type correlation factors
     lambda <- sqrt(n[vi]/(gn+1));
     
     ## diagonal elements of the covariance-matrix
     vd.st <- sapply(1:nc, function(arg) ssq(pairRanks[[arg]]-(gn[arg]+1)/2)) / 
       (n[vi]*n[vj]*(gn-1));
     
     ## mark and correct zero variances for further calculations
     singular.st <- (vd.st==0);
     vd.st[singular.st] <- 0.00000001;
     
     ## standard-deviation
     std.st <- sqrt(vd.st/gn);
     
     ## teststatistic
     t.st <- (pd-0.5)*sqrt(gn/vd.st);
     
     
     ## Calculate the correlation-matrices (for both, BF and Steel) 
     ##    
     rho.bf <- rho.st <- diag(nc);
     for (x in 1:(nc-1))
     {
       for (y in (x+1):nc)
       {
         i <- vi[x]; j <- vj[x];
         v <- vi[y]; w <- vj[y];
         p <- c(i==v, j==w, i==w, j==v);
         if (sum(p)==1) 
         {      
           cl <- list(
             function()  (t(dji[[x]]) %*% dji[[y]]) / (n[j]*n[w]*n[i]*(n[i]-1)),
             function()  (t(dij[[x]]) %*% dij[[y]]) / (n[i]*n[v]*n[j]*(n[j]-1)),
             function() -(t(dji[[x]]) %*% dij[[y]]) / (n[i]*n[w]*n[i]*(n[i]-1)),
             function() -(t(dij[[x]]) %*% dji[[y]]) / (n[j]*n[v]*n[j]*(n[j]-1))
           );
           case <- (1:4)[p];
           rho.bf[x,y] <- rho.bf[y,x] <- 
             sqrt(gn[x]*gn[y]) / sqrt(vd.bf[x]*vd.bf[y]) * cl[[case]]()
           ;
           rho.st[x,y] <- rho.st[y,x] <- 
             {if (case>2) -1 else 1}*lambda[x]*lambda[y]
           ;
         }
       }
     }
     rho.bf <- force.ps(rho.bf);
     rho.st <- force.ps(rho.st);
     
     
     ## Calculate the p-values     (BF and Steel) 
     ##
     p1s.bf <- 1 - z.dist(t.bf, corr=rho.bf, df=df, sides=1);
     p2s.bf <- 1 - z.dist(t.bf, corr=rho.bf, df=df, sides=2);
     
     p1s.st <- 1 - z.dist(t.st, corr=rho.st, sides=1);
     p2s.st <- 1 - z.dist(t.st, corr=rho.st, sides=2);
     
     
     ## Calculate the confidence-limits (BF and Steel) 
     ##
     z.bf <- z.quantile(1-alpha, corr=rho.bf, df=df, sides=2);
     lcl.bf <- pd - std.bf*z.bf;
     ucl.bf <- pd + std.bf*z.bf;
     
     z.st <- z.quantile(1-alpha, corr=rho.st, sides=2);
     lcl.st <- pd - std.st*z.st;
     ucl.st <- pd + std.st*z.st;
     
     
     ## Output 
     
     ## Create the result-datastructures 
     ##    
     dataStructure <- data.frame("group index"=1:a, 
                                 "class level"=fl, 
                                 "nobs"=n
     );
     
     test.bf <- data.frame("cmp"=cmpid, 
                           "gn"=gn, 
                           "effect"=pd,
                           "lower.cl"=lcl.bf,
                           "upper.cl"=ucl.bf,
                           "variance"=vd.bf, 
                           "std"=std.bf, 
                           "statistic"=t.bf, 
                           "p-value 1s"=p1s.bf, 
                           "p-value 2s"=p2s.bf, 
                           "zero"=singular.bf
     ); 
     
     test.st <- data.frame("cmp"=cmpid, 
                           "gn"=gn, 
                           "effect"=pd, 
                           "lower.cl"=lcl.st,
                           "upper.cl"=ucl.st,
                           "variance"=vd.st, 
                           "std"=std.st, 
                           "statistic"=t.st, 
                           "p-value 1s"=p1s.st, 
                           "p-value 2s"=p2s.st, 
                           "zero"=singular.st
     ); 
     
     result <- list("data"=dataset,
                    "info"=dataStructure, 
                    "corr"=list("BF"=rho.bf, "Steel"=rho.st),
                    "test"=list("BF"=test.bf, "Steel"=test.st),
                    "control"=control,
                    "df.method"=dfm,
                    "df"=df,
                    "alpha"=alpha
     );
     
     class(result) <- "npmc";
     
     return (result);
     
   }
 

 
 ### with trend line 
 krus_BF <- function(data, groups, values, p = 0.05) {
   stat_kruskal <- NULL
   stat_BF <- NULL
   abc_list <- NULL
   
   #统计检验
   for (i in groups) {
     for (j in values) {
       
       #Kruskal-Wallis 检验，整体差异
       dat <- data[c(i, j)]
       names(dat) <- c('class', 'var')
       dat$class <- factor(dat$class)
       fit <- kruskal.test(var~class, dat)
       p_value <- fit$p.value
       
       #获取 Kruskal-Wallis 检验 p 值
       if (p_value < 0.001) sig <- '***'
       else if (p_value >= 0.001 & p_value < 0.01) sig <- '**'
       else if (p_value >= 0.01 & p_value < 0.05) sig <- '*'
       else sig <- ''
       stat_kruskal <- rbind(stat_kruskal, c(paste(i, j, sep = '/'), p_value, sig))
       
       #Behrens-Fisher 检验（npmc 包），非参数多重比较
       BF_test <- npmc(dataset = dat, control=NULL, df = 2, alpha = 0.05)
       BF <- BF_test$test$BF
       info <- BF_test$info
       
       BF$group <- paste(i, j, sep = '/')
       for (l in 1:nrow(BF)) {
         x <- strsplit(as.vector(BF[l,'cmp']), '-')[[1]]
         BF[l,'class1'] <- rownames(info)[which(info$group.index == x[1])]
         BF[l,'class2'] <- rownames(info)[which(info$group.index == x[2])]
       }
       stat_BF <- rbind(stat_BF, BF[c(12:14, 2:11)])
       
       #Behrens-Fisher 检验 p 值矩阵获取
       stat_p <- BF[c(13, 14, 10)]
       stat_p1 <- stat_p[c(2, 1, 3)]
       names(stat_p1)[1:2] <- c('class1', 'class2')
       stat_p <- rbind(stat_p, stat_p1)
       stat_p <- dcast(stat_p, class1~class2, value.var = 'p.value.2s')
       rownames(stat_p) <- stat_p$class1
       
       #计算各组中位数
       abc_ij <- aggregate(dat$var, by = list(dat$class), FUN = mean)
       abc_ij$group <- i
       abc_ij$var <- j
       abc_ij <- abc_ij[c(3, 4, 1, 2)]
       names(abc_ij) <- c('group', 'var', 'class', 'median')
       
       #根据中位数和 p 值，手动添加显著性标记“abc”
       abc_ij <- abc_ij[order(abc_ij$median, decreasing = TRUE), ]
       class <- as.vector(abc_ij$class)
       
       m = 1; n = 2; l = 1
       abc_ij[m,'sig'] <- letters[l]
       while (n < length(class)) {
         for (n in (m+1):length(class)) {
           if (stat_p[class[m],class[n]] < p) {
             abc_ij[n,'sig'] <- letters[l+1]
             if (n - m != 1) {
               for (x in (m+1):(n-1)) {
                 if (stat_p[class[x],class[n]] < p) abc_ij[x,'sig'] <- letters[l]
                 else abc_ij[x,'sig'] <- paste(letters[l], letters[l+1], sep = '')
               }
             }
             l = l + 1
             m = n
             break
           }
         }
       }
       abc_ij[(m:n),'sig'] <- letters[l]
       
       abc_list <- rbind(abc_list, abc_ij)
     }
   }
   
   #ggplot2 作图，箱线图
   data <- melt(data[c(groups, values)], id = groups)
   data <- melt(data, id = c('variable', 'value'))
   data <- data[c(3, 1, 4, 2)]
   names(data) <- c('group', 'var', 'class', 'value')
   
   data$type <- data$class
 # data['type'][data['type'] == 4 | data['type'] == 7 | data['type'] == 9] <- 'DI'
   data['type'][data['type'] == 11 | data['type'] == 12 | data['type'] == 14 | data['type'] == 15 | data['type'] == 17] <- 'SI'
   
   value_max <- aggregate(data$value, by = list(data$group, data$var), FUN = max)
   names(value_max) <- c('group', 'var', 'value')
   value_max <- merge(value_max, abc_list[-4], by = c('group', 'var'))
   
   
   #cgf
  # myPalette = c("#dadaeb","#bcbddc","#9e9ac8","#fee08b","#fdae61","#f46d43","#ffffbf","#e6f598","#abdda4","#66c2a5","#3288bd") #si
   
   #data$class <- factor(data$class, levels = c("SD","OsF","IsF","4","7","9", "11","12","14","15","17"))
   #see
   # myPalette = c('#D9D9D9','#80B1D3','#FDB462','#B0DB67')
   #data$class <- factor(data$class, levels = c("Sd","Nbc","Bc","Nr"))
   
   # myPalette = c("#dadaeb","#fee08b","#fdae61","#f46d43","#ffffbf","#e6f598","#abdda4","#66c2a5","#3288bd") 
   
   # data$class <- factor(data$class, levels = c("SD","4","7","9", "11","12","14","15","17"))
   
   #cgf without OSF and ISF
 # myPalette = c("#dadaeb","#fee08b","#fdae61","#f46d43","#ffffbf","#e6f598","#abdda4","#66c2a5","#3288bd") #si
   
  # data$class <- factor(data$class, levels = c("SD","4","7","9", "11","12","14","15","17"))
   
   #cgf for sd and si
   myPalette = c("#dadaeb","#ffffbf","#e6f598","#abdda4","#66c2a5","#3288bd") #si
   
   data$class <- factor(data$class, levels = c("SD","11","12","14","15","17"))
   
   # cgf sd di
  # myPalette = c("#dadaeb","#fee08b","#fdae61","#f46d43") #si
   
   #data$class <- factor(data$class, levels = c("SD","4","7","9"))
   
   plot_box_g <- ggplot(data = data, aes(x = class, y = value, fill = class)) +
     scale_fill_manual(values = myPalette) +
     facet_grid(. ~ var) + facet_wrap(~ var, scales = "free_y",ncol = 6) +
     theme(strip.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(3.5,0.50,3.5,0.50,"cm"))) +
     geom_boxplot(aes(x=class, y=value,group=class),outlier.shape = NA) + 
     geom_beeswarm(color = "black", size = 0.5, alpha = 0.7,dodge.width = 0.05) +
     geom_smooth(data = subset(data,type=='SI'), aes(group=1), method = "glm",color = "#225EA8", se=F,alpha = 0.8) +
     #geom_smooth(data = subset(data,type=='DI'), aes(group=1), method = "glm",color = "#B34300", se=F,alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text(data = value_max, aes(label = sig, y = value + 0.05*value), size = 8) +
     theme_bw()+ ylab("") + xlab('') +
     theme(legend.position = "none",
           panel.grid=element_blank()) +
     theme(text=element_text(size = 25)) +
     theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 25, colour = 'black')) +
     theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 25, colour = 'black')) +
     theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill="#FFFFFF")) +
     theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 32)) 
   
   plot_box_m <- ggplot(data = data, aes(x = class, y = value, fill = class)) +
     scale_fill_manual(values = myPalette) +
     facet_grid(. ~ var) + facet_wrap(~ var, scales = "free_y",ncol = 6) +
     theme(strip.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(3.5,0.50,3.5,0.50,"cm"))) +
     geom_boxplot(aes(x=class, y=value,group=class)) + geom_beeswarm(color = "black", size = 0.2, alpha = 0.4,dodge.width = 0.05) +
     stat_summary(data = subset(data,type=='SI'),fun=median, geom="line", aes(group=1), color = "#225EA8", size=1) +
   #  stat_summary(data = subset(data,type=='DI'),fun=median, geom="line", aes(group=1), color = "#B34300", size=1) +
   #  geom_text(data = value_max, aes(label = sig, y = value + 0.05*value), size = 8) +
     theme_bw()+ ylab("") + xlab('') +
     theme(legend.position = "none",
           panel.grid=element_blank()) +
     theme(text=element_text(size = 25)) +
     theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 25, colour = 'black')) +
     theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 25, colour = 'black')) +
     theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill="#FFFFFF")) +
     theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 32)) 
   
   #return
   stat_kruskal <- data.frame(stat_kruskal, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
   names(stat_kruskal) <- c('group', 'kruskal_pvalue', 'sig')
   stat_kruskal$kruskal_pvalue <- as.numeric(stat_kruskal$kruskal_pvalue)
   
   stat_BF[which(stat_BF$p.value.2s < 0.001),'sig.2s'] <- '***'
   stat_BF[which(stat_BF$p.value.2s >= 0.001 & stat_BF$p.value.2s < 0.01),'sig.2s'] <- '**'
   stat_BF[which(stat_BF$p.value.2s >= 0.01 & stat_BF$p.value.2s < 0.05),'sig.2s'] <- '*'
   stat_BF[which(stat_BF$p.value.2s >= 0.05),'sig.2s'] <- ''
   
   list(data = value_max, stat = list(kruskal = stat_kruskal, BF_p = stat_BF, BF_abc = abc_list), plot_g = plot_box_g, plot_m = plot_box_m)
 }
```

```{r c-means}
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 25, colour = 'black')) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 25, colour = 'black')) +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank()) + ylab("Scaled Values") +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size = 25,colour = 'black')) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",panel.grid=element_blank())
```
